name: India: Kashmir, Manipur and the Maoist belt

status.en: 303 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, 15% fewer than the week before, most of them in Delhi, Mumbai and Hyderabad.
status.nb: 303 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, 15 prosent færre enn uken før, flest i Delhi, Mumbai og Hyderabad.

summary.en: The newly released leaders of the “cockroach” movement have reignited street protests in Delhi, while fresh Kuki‑Naga clashes in Manipur have left nine dead and prompted the chief minister to call for peace. Violence remains high in Kashmir and the Maoist‑affected belt, adding to overall volatility across the country. The resurgence of protests and the spike in Manipur killings represent a sharp escalation compared with the earlier assessment, which noted only a general increase in tension. The UCDP recorded 437 battle‑related deaths in 2024, underscoring the broader conflict intensity.
summary.nb: De nyutnevnte lederne for “kakerlakk”-bevegelsen har gjenopplivet gateprotestene i Delhi, mens ferske Kuki‑Naga‑konflikter i Manipur har etterlatt ni døde og fått statsministeren til å oppfordre til fred. Voldsnivået forblir høyt i Kashmir og i den maoist‑påvirkede beltet, noe som øker den generelle ustabiliteten i landet. Gjenoppblomstringen av protester og oppgangen i drapene i Manipur representerer en skarp opptrapping sammenlignet med den tidligere vurderingen, som kun bemerket en generell økning i spenning. UCDP registrerte 437 dødsfall i kamprelaterte hendelser i 2024, og understreker den bredere konfliktintensiteten.

background.title: Kashmir conflict
background.extract: The Kashmir conflict is a territorial conflict over the Kashmir region, primarily between India and Pakistan, and also between China and India in the northeastern portion of the region. The conflict started after the partition of India in 1947 as both India and Pakistan claimed the entirety of the former princely state of Jammu and Kashmir. It is a dispute over the region that escalated into three wars between India and Pakistan and several other armed skirmishes. India controls approximately 55% of the land area of the region that includes Jammu, the Kashmir Valley, most of Ladakh, the Siachen Glacier, and 70% of its population; Pakistan controls approximately 30% of the land area that includes Azad Kashmir and Gilgit-Baltistan; and China controls the remaining 15% of the land area that includes the Aksai Chin region, the mostly uninhabited Trans-Karakoram Tract, and part of the Demchok sector.
